A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CODE-CL. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices are readable and support matching content across revisions and relocations. Internal inconsistencies in v2's settings do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CODE-CL accuracy and backward-transfer results on four benchmarks in Tables 1–2, plus experiments varying K in Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 reports original CODE-CL benchmark results, relative forward transfer, overlapping-class evaluation, resource measurements, and parameter studies in the main text and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The conceptor objective, overlap threshold, top-K shared-direction mixing, projected gradient updates, and OR consolidation are retained. The revised pseudocode corrects its effective-weight sign to match the equation already present in v1; it does not establish a new learning procedure.

E1.justification: v2 removes Permuted MNIST, eliminating the sole domain-incremental evaluation. It adds OL-CIFAR100: seven tasks covering 50 classes, with classes recurring across tasks. Split CIFAR100, Split miniImageNet, and 5-Datasets remain, substantially shifting coverage toward overlapping-class task sequences.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CUBER and DFGP across all three retained benchmarks, API on miniImageNet and 5-Datasets, and TRGP+SD on the two Split benchmarks. It also adds an SGP comparison on 5-Datasets, previously absent. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces GPM-relative FWT evaluation and runtime/GPU-memory measurements, and reports reproducing GPM, TRGP, and SGP rather than importing their scores. Section 4.1.2 changes aperture from 8 to 16 for miniImageNet and 4 to 8 for 5-Datasets, although Appendix Table 9 retains the old values. Retained benchmark splits, architectures, and epoch limits otherwise match.

E4.justification: v2 adds aperture and threshold sensitivity studies, taskwise accuracy/forgetting analysis, measured resource comparisons, and an overlapping-class study. Existing K analyses are largely replotted or relocated, including the 5-Datasets analysis in Appendix Table 6; the Permuted MNIST K study is removed.

E5.justification: Five-trial mean ± standard deviation reporting is retained, with no stated increase in runs. However, v1's K-study boxplots explicitly represent five independent runs, whereas v2 Figure 5 uses shaded bands without defining their statistic, changing the clarity and form of graphical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces CODE-CL's miniImageNet accuracy of 68.83% with 71.16% and 5-Datasets accuracy of 93.32% with 93.51%, alongside changed stated apertures; these are not established same-setting gains. GPM, TRGP, and SGP scores also change. New results include relative FWT, OL-CIFAR100 accuracy of 76.89%, resource measurements, and sensitivity results; Permuted MNIST results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's aperture-adaptation definition, corrects the SVD expression to factor X transpose rather than X, defines GPM-relative FWT, and extends memory-complexity reasoning to CUBER. The main conceptor equations and rank-deficient AND construction remain; no new proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution of combining retention with forward transfer remains. v2 adds quantified headline claims of about 1.15% better final accuracy and up to 1.18% improved relative FWT, and explicitly claims comparative FWT superiority in its abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of aperture's retention/plasticity tradeoff, threshold and K performance/memory tradeoffs, overlapping-class transfer, and measured overhead relative to GPM and SGP. It removes v1's explanation attributing contrasting K/BWT trends to differences in dataset distributions, substantially revising the discussion of mechanisms and practical limits.

D1.justification: v2 adds provenance for reproduced baselines and measured runtime/memory information. Its condensed pseudocode omits v1's explicit initialization of M and detailed scheduling loops, while most architecture, preprocessing, hardware, and software details remain. The conflicting aperture values in Section 4.1.2 and Table 9 weaken reproducibility.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially refocuses positioning on transfer limitations and fine-grained direction selection, adding discussion of CUBER, API, DFGP, and space decoupling. General regularization/expansion coverage is compressed, and v1's named explanation of Conceptor-Aided Backpropagation disappears, although that work remains cited.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, results discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Section 3 is reorganized into problem formulation and approach, condensed pseudocode moves into the main text, and the appendices are restructured around new ablation material and relocated experimental setup.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is completely redesigned as a three-stage singular-value schematic. Existing K boxplots become curves and an appendix table. v2 also adds taskwise accuracy, resource, and aperture figures; expands comparison tables; and introduces FWT, overlapping-class, and appendix ablation tables.

improvement.justification: v1 largely supported its central transfer and efficiency claims through final accuracy and asymptotic memory analysis. v2 makes these claims substantially more assessable through defined GPM-relative FWT, overlapping-class tests, measured resource costs, broader comparisons, and additional sensitivity studies. Dropping Permuted MNIST reduces coverage, and conflicting aperture documentation weakens reproducibility, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
